title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook (2026)
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Purpose and scope:
This document defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices for production services (examples: redwood-api, inference-runtime, routing-proxy, batcher). It covers the incident lifecycle, roles and responsibilities, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations, game day guidance, and standard status page / customer communication templates.

Goals:
- Restore customer-facing functionality quickly and safely.
- Minimize blast radius and data exposure.
- Capture timeline and root cause for continuous improvement.
- Keep customers informed with timely, accurate messages.

Audience:
- SREs, service owners, product engineers, support, and customer success.

Key definitions and SLAs:
- Incident: any event that materially reduces service quality or violates an SLO.
- Incident severity levels (use these for routing and comms):
  - Sev1 (P0): Total service outage or data-loss affecting most customers. Target MTTR: <1 hour. Exec and customer comms required within 30 minutes.
  - Sev2 (P1): Significant degradation (e.g., API errors >5% or P95 latency >3x target) affecting many customers. Target MTTR: <4 hours. Initial comms within 60 minutes.
  - Sev3 (P2): Partial degradation or isolated customer impact with a workaround. Target MTTR: <24 hours.
  - Sev4 (P3): Maintenance, scheduled changes, or minor issues. No SLO breach.

Service SLO examples (production reference):
- redwood-api availability: 99.95% monthly.
- inference-runtime P95 latency (text generation, 256 tokens): <250ms.
- embeddings API error rate: <0.1% per week.
(See related SLO page for full list and alert thresholds.)

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detect 
  - Source: monitoring alerts (Prometheus -> Alertmanager/PagerDuty), customer reports, automated health checks, canary failures, or on-call observation.
2) Triage / Declare
  - On-call engineer reviews alerts, checks dashboards and logs, and determines severity. If impact meets Sev1/Sev2 criteria, declare an incident and open an incident channel (Slack #incident-<id>) and incident doc.
3) Assemble response team
  - Roles: Incident Commander (IC), Primary Responder, Scribe, Communications Lead, Service Owners.
4) Mitigate / Stabilize
  - Apply runbook steps or roll back recent deploys. If unknown cause, apply safe mitigations (rate-limit, circuit-breaker, failover).
5) Restore
  - Restore service, validate with synthetic tests and customers.
6) Communicate
  - Publish status updates to internal channel, status page, customer success, and execs as required (see templates).
7) Post-incident
  - Conduct a blameless postmortem within 48 hours (initial draft) and a final RCA within 7 days. Create action items with owners and deadlines.

Incident roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): sets priorities, coordinates response, declares incident severity, and authorizes escalations.
- Primary Responder: drives technical troubleshooting and implements fixes.
- Scribe: records timeline, commands, decisions, and customer-facing messages.
- Communications Lead: prepares status page and customer messages; coordinates with Customer Success.
- Service Owner: responsible for long-term remediation and postmortem follow-up items.
- Pager Duty: on-call roster and escalation policies (link to PagerDuty schedule).

Runbook structure (single-runbook template, use per-service):
- Title: (e.g. inference-runtime high GPU utilization)
- Scope/when to use: symptoms and alert IDs.
- Owner: team and individual oncall rota.
- Prerequisites: required tools and dashboards (links), permissions, emergency keys.
- Detection: queries and PromQL/CLI examples.
- Immediate mitigation steps (ordered checklist):
  1. Verify alert: timestamp, affected regions, service health.
  2. Check recent deploys: git rev, release pipeline.
  3. Reproduce locally if safe: recommend synthetic curl/SDK command.
  4. Apply mitigation A: e.g., scale up pool or disable feature flag.
  5. If mitigation fails, failover to secondary region.
- Escalation: who to call and when (pager escalation matrix).
- Post-incident: required logs, tl;dr summary, and postmortem link.

Example runbook: redwood-api 502 surge
- Symptoms: sudden spike in 502 responses across gateway, alert: api.5xx.rate > 2% for 5m
- Immediate steps: 
  1. IC: open channel #incident-api-<id>, set severity.
  2. Primary: check gateway logs (kubectl logs -l app=gateway --since=10m) and upstream service health (curl -s http://inference-runtime/health).
  3. If error from inference-runtime, restart pod: kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n production.
  4. If restart ineffective, scale inference-runtime replicas: kubectl scale deployment/inference-runtime --replicas=10 -n production.
  5. If sustained memory OOMs, revert last deploy: deploy rollback command.
  6. Communications: publish status update (template below).

Escalation matrix (summary):
- On-call engineer -> Service Owner (10 mins) -> Eng SRE lead (30 mins) -> VP Eng (60 mins for Sev1).
- PagerDuty steps are configured in the on-call schedule with automatic escalation.

On-call rotations and expectations:
- Rotation model: 7-day primary on-call, followed by 7-day secondary (double coverage during business hours).
- Primary: responsible for paging and first response 24/7.
- Secondary: escalation for unresolved or complex incidents.
- Shift handoffs: mandatory handoff note in #oncall-handoffs Slack channel with outstanding items, ongoing incidents, and pager status.
- Time-off and swaps: use the on-call scheduling tool (PagerDuty) and notify your team at least 48 hours in advance.
- On-call compensation and training: follow People Ops policy (link).

Hand-off checklist (to post to #oncall-handoffs):
- Date/time of handoff.
- Active incidents and current status.
- Recent deploys and goroutines (link to build).
- Any escalations or outstanding action items.
- Test synthetic checks I ran and their pass/fail.

Game days (periodic rehearsals):
- Purpose: validate runbooks, alerting, and cross-team coordination.
- Frequency: quarterly for critical services, semiannual for secondary services.
- Typical agenda:
  1. Pre-brief and goals (30m).
  2. Run scenario (1-2 hours): e.g., region outage, high error rate, performance regression after deploy.
  3. Post-game debrief (1 hour): what worked, gaps in runbook, alert tuning, and action items.
- Metrics collected: time-to-detect, time-to-declare, time-to-restore, communication latency.

Postmortem process and template (blameless):
- Timeline: start/stop times, detection, mitigation, and restore actions with 1-5 minute granularity during high-activity windows.
- Impact: affected customers, affected endpoints, data loss (yes/no), estimated downtime.
- Root cause analysis: concise statement of root cause and contributing factors.
- Detection and monitoring gaps: alerts missing or too noisy.
- Corrective actions: short-term mitigations and long-term fixes with owners and due dates.
- Lessons learned and follow-up: cross-team action items and metrics to prevent recurrence.
- Approval: Service Owner and Eng SRE lead sign-off.

Postmortem template (fields to include):
- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Timeline (table or bullet list)
- Impact summary
- Root cause
- Remediation and action items (owner + due date)
- Follow-up verification plan
- Links: runbooks, dashboards, deploys, logs

Customer and status page communication templates (use placeholders, keep them concise and factual):
- Status page phased messages (short):
  - Investigating: "We are aware of elevated errors affecting the redwood-api in [region]. Our team is investigating. No workaround is available at this time. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."
  - Identified: "We have identified the cause as excessive load on inference-runtime. Engineers are applying mitigations including scaling and rate-limiting. Impact: increased 5xx errors for some customers in [region]."
  - Monitoring: "The fix has been applied and metrics are improving. We are monitoring to ensure stability. If you continue to see errors, please contact support@redwood.ai with Incident ID: INCIDENT-<id>."
  - Resolved: "Service has been restored. We are continuing to monitor. A post-incident summary will be published within 7 days."

- Customer email template (for major incidents):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident INCIDENT-<id>: Service disruption affecting <feature/service>
  Body:
  Hello <Customer Name>,

  We wanted to let you know that on <date/time> Redwood experienced an incident impacting <service>. Impact: <brief impact statement>.

  What we did: <brief mitigation summary>.
  Current status: <monitoring / resolved>.
  What we're doing next: <RCA timeline and action items>.

  If you have questions or need help, contact your CSM or support@redwood.ai and reference INCIDENT-<id>.

  Sincerely,
  Redwood Support

Internal exec notification template (for Sev1):
  Subject: [Alert] Sev1 Incident INCIDENT-<id>  <short summary>
  Body:
  Summary: <one-line impact>
  Time detected: <time>
  Action being taken: <actions>
  Current ETA to restore: <estimate>
  Next update: <time>

Status page guidelines:
- Update cadence: every 30 minutes for Sev1, every 60 minutes for Sev2 until in monitoring.
- Keep messages factual, avoid speculation, and include incident ID, services affected, regions, and customer impact.
- Coordination: Communications Lead drafts message; IC approves before publishing.

Tools and integrations (examples):
- PagerDuty: paging and escalation.
- Slack: incident channels (#incident-<id>), #oncall-handoffs, #postmortems.
- Confluence: runbooks and postmortems.
- Statuspage (or internal status tool): public incident posts.
- Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and traces in Jaeger/Tempo.
- CI/CD: links to recent deploys and commit SHAs.

Runbook and postmortem hygiene checklist (required before closing incident):
- Complete timeline in incident doc.
- Attach relevant logs and dashboards.
- Create postmortem draft within 48 hours.
- Assign owners and due dates for remediation.
- Close incident only after IC and Service Owner sign-off.

Training and onboarding:
- New on-call engineers must complete a one-week on-call shadowing and two runbook walkthroughs.
- Quarterly training includes a mandatory game day and incident simulation.

Appendix: Useful commands and queries
- Check pods: kubectl get pods -n production -l service=inference-runtime
- View logs: kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n production --since=15m
- PromQL: rate(http_requests_total{job="redwood-api",code=~"5.."}[5m]) / rate(http_requests_total{job="redwood-api"}[5m])

Contacts and escalation phone list (obfuscated here; use internal directory):
- Eng SRE on-call (primary): see PagerDuty schedule
- Service Owners: inference-runtime: Jordan Patel; redwood-api: Marcus Li

End of playbook.
